headline: The service started this run because baseline loop 164687 (width 200, f* 0.65) ended as FAILED. It and four earlier failed baseline loops stopped under the loop's own rules: the unmodified engine hit a sphere overlap. Nothing needs relaunching. Four of the ten width-200 baseline loops broke on their first step, against one at width 100, and f* 0.65 covered a narrower range of Gamma than in the paper's box (2.4 to 3.9 against 2.25 to 4.1, one seed).

experiments.question: Where does the unmodified engine with friction stop on a Gamma loop in the box twice as wide, compared with the paper's box?
experiments.what_was_done: Read the fetched per-step summaries of the five baseline loops that have ended on Hatteras and compared them with the same loops in the paper's box. Collected into an interim evidence file; the experiment's outcome waits for the other five loops.
experiments.result: At f* 0.65 the loop went down to Gamma 2.4 (overlap at 2.35), turned, climbed to 3.9 and hit an overlap at 3.95, using 46 CPU-hours. The paper's box at the same f* reached 2.25 and 4.1. At f* 0.84, 0.33, 0.30 and 0.27 the loop broke in its first step at Gamma 3.0 after zero or one of fifty cycles; in the paper's box only 0.27 broke there. No completed step gained energy or failed the audit. A 25-cycle step cost a median of 0.91 CPU-hours, about five and a half times the paper's box.
experiments.takeaway: The wider box gives the unmodified engine four times as many particles that can overlap, so a narrower working range is what one expects. With one seed this is not yet a measured size effect. The cost agrees with the cost holds (4.7 to 5.6 times).

experiments.question: (Collected in passing) Why did the width-200 nudge loop at f* 0.27 end?
experiments.what_was_done: Read its Slurm log and first-step summary.
experiments.result: It hit the four CPU-hour cap of its 50-cycle first step at Gamma 3.0 after 49 cycles, so the loop has no data past its start.
experiments.takeaway: The caps are the ones Chris kept on Nov 22, so I did not relaunch it.

questions.question: The width-200 nudge loop at f* 0.27 stopped one cycle short of finishing its first step (cap of four CPU-hours). Should I restart it from its start with a higher first-step cap, for example eight CPU-hours?
questions.why_it_matters: Without it the nudge has no width-200 data at the lowest frequency; the other nine nudge loops are running.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Leave it stopped, as the Nov 22 reply kept the caps.

proposed_directions.direction: Rerun the four width-200 baseline loops that broke on their first step with a second seed, to tell a size effect from bad luck in the start.
proposed_directions.rationale: Four of ten broke against one of ten at width 100; with one seed each, this could be the start state rather than the box.

proposed_directions.direction: When all E0076 loops end, compare floor and ceiling per f* with width 100 in one table.
proposed_directions.rationale: That gives the baseline's working range against box size, which the comparison with the nudge needs.
